tasks.title: Stable Deduplication
tasks.description: Write a function `stable_dedup(items)` that removes duplicate elements from a list while strictly preserving the insertion order of their first appearance.
tasks.input_spec: A list of primitive items (integers or strings).
tasks.output_spec: A list with duplicates removed in original first-seen order.
tasks.expected_trap: Converting to `list(set(items))` loses original insertion order. Must track seen items using a set while preserving list sequence or use OrderedDict/dict.fromkeys.

test_cases.description: Standard list with multiple duplicates

test_cases.name: String sequence with duplicates
test_cases.description: String elements deduplicated

test_cases.name: Already unique list
test_cases.description: No duplicates present

test_cases.name: All identical elements
test_cases.description: Entire list collapses to single element

test_cases.name: Empty list boundary
test_cases.description: Empty input should return empty list

tasks.title: Bracket Matcher with String Literals
tasks.description: Write a function `is_bracket_balanced(s)` that determines if parentheses `()`, square brackets `[]`, and curly braces `{}` are properly matched and nested. Critical rule: Any brackets enclosed within double quotes `"..."` are treated as literal text and MUST be ignored during bracket balancing.
tasks.input_spec: A string `s` containing characters, quotes, and brackets.
tasks.expected_trap: Standard stack bracket matchers fail to ignore brackets inside quotes, misinterpreting literal characters like '"}"' as closing tokens.

test_cases.name: Simple balanced brackets
test_cases.description: Standard nested brackets

test_cases.name: Mismatched brackets
test_cases.description: Direct mismatch

test_cases.name: Quoted opening bracket inside pair
test_cases.description: Internal bracket is inside double quotes and ignored

test_cases.name: Quoted closing brace inside brackets
test_cases.description: Closing brace inside quotes must not prematurely close bracket

test_cases.name: Empty string boundary
test_cases.description: Empty string is vacuously balanced

tasks.title: Max Stock Profit with Cooldown
tasks.description: Write a function `max_profit_cooldown(prices)` finding the maximum profit you can achieve given an array where `prices[i]` is the stock price on day `i`. Rule: You may complete as many transactions as you like, but after you sell your stock, you cannot buy stock on the next day (i.e. cooldown 1 day).
tasks.input_spec: A list of non-negative integer stock prices.
tasks.output_spec: An integer representing the maximum profit achievable.
tasks.expected_trap: Greedy buy-low-sell-high algorithms fail because selling immediately may trigger an undesirable cooldown that forfeits a larger profit on the next peak.

test_cases.name: Canonical DP case
test_cases.description: Buy at 1, sell at 3 (profit=2); cooldown; buy at 0, sell at 2 (profit=2) -> optimal total = 3

test_cases.name: Strictly declining prices
test_cases.description: No profitable transactions possible

test_cases.name: Monotonically increasing prices
test_cases.description: Buy at 1, sell at 4

test_cases.name: Single price point
test_cases.description: Cannot complete transaction with one price

test_cases.name: Empty price list
test_cases.description: Empty array profit is 0

tasks.title: Deep Key Flattener with Null Preservation
tasks.description: Write a function `flatten_dict(d, parent_key='', sep='.')` that flattens a nested dictionary. Keys should be concatenated with `sep`. Explicit `None` / `null` values must be preserved in the flattened dictionary rather than omitted.
tasks.input_spec: A nested dictionary with string keys.
tasks.output_spec: A flat dictionary mapping dotted key paths to leaf values.
tasks.expected_trap: Using truthy checks like `if val:` unintentionally drops explicit `None`, `False`, or `0` values from the flattened output.

test_cases.name: Nested dictionary with None value
test_cases.description: Null leaf must be retained

test_cases.name: Falsy values preserved (False and 0)
test_cases.description: False and 0 must not be treated as empty

test_cases.name: Already flat dictionary
test_cases.description: No nesting present

test_cases.name: Empty dictionary input
test_cases.description: Empty dict should yield empty dict

tasks.title: Exact Currency Splitter without Penny Drift
tasks.description: Write a function `split_currency(total_cents, num_recipients)` that splits an integer number of cents among `num_recipients` as evenly as possible. The sum of the allocated parts MUST equal `total_cents` exactly. Any remainder cents are distributed one-by-one to the first recipients.
tasks.output_spec: A list of integers representing the cents assigned to each recipient in order.
tasks.expected_trap: Floating-point division `total / num` loses fractional cents due to IEEE-754 precision issues or integer truncations that fail to allocate remainder cents.

test_cases.name: 100 cents across 3 recipients
test_cases.description: 1 remainder cent given to first recipient

test_cases.name: 10 cents across 4 recipients
test_cases.description: 2 remainder cents given to first two recipients

test_cases.name: Even division with zero remainder
test_cases.description: Exact divide

test_cases.name: Zero total cents
test_cases.description: Zero split returns zeros

test_cases.name: Fewer cents than recipients
test_cases.description: Some recipients receive 0 cents

tasks.title: Sliding Window Maximum
tasks.description: Write a function `max_sliding_window(nums, k)` that returns the maximum value in each sliding window of size `k` moving from left to right across the list `nums`.
tasks.input_spec: A list of integers `nums` and an integer window size `k` (1 <= k <= len(nums)).
tasks.output_spec: A list of integers containing maximum values of each window.
tasks.expected_trap: Off-by-one errors in window range boundaries, especially when k=1 or k equals the length of nums, or incorrect handling of all-negative sequences.

test_cases.description: Classic sliding window sequence

test_cases.name: Window size k = 1
test_cases.description: k=1 should return the input list unchanged

test_cases.name: Window size k equals list length
test_cases.description: Single window spanning whole list

test_cases.name: All negative numbers
test_cases.description: Negative numbers must be compared correctly without zero default

tasks.title: Strict Roman Numeral Validator and Parser
tasks.description: Write a function `parse_roman_strict(s)` that converts a valid Roman numeral string `s` into an integer (1 to 3999). CRITICAL: If the string is invalid Roman notation (e.g. invalid repetitions like 'IIII', 'VV', illegal subtractive pairs like 'IC' or 'IL', or incorrect ordering), return -1.
tasks.input_spec: A string `s` representing a putative Roman numeral.
tasks.output_spec: Integer value if strictly valid, or -1 if invalid notation.
tasks.expected_trap: Standard additive-subtractive algorithms blindly calculate 4 for 'IIII' or 99 for 'IC' instead of enforcing Roman grammar constraints (re-encoding canonical check).

test_cases.name: Invalid repetition 'IIII'
test_cases.description: More than 3 identical additive characters is invalid

test_cases.name: Invalid subtractive pair 'IC'
test_cases.description: I can only precede V and X, not C

test_cases.name: Invalid repeat of non-repeatable symbol 'VV'
test_cases.description: V, L, D cannot be repeated

tasks.title: Run-Length Encoding with Single-Char Guard
tasks.description: Write a function `run_length_encode(text)` that encodes consecutive identical characters as `<char><count>` ONLY when count >= 2. Single characters must remain without a count (e.g., 'A', NOT 'A1').
tasks.expected_trap: Naive run-length encoding appends '1' to single characters, transforming 'ABC' into 'A1B1C1' which expands rather than compresses the text.
